subject: Discovery recap: Brightlane POC engagement charter & risk compact
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Turner <maya@brightlane.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@brightlane.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Brightlane POC engagement charter & risk compact

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on goals. Per our conversation I captured a lean engagement charter below so we can move to a technical kickoff quickly. Attached: Brightlane-POC-charter-v1.pdf and a sample data schema (brightlane-sample-schema.csv).

Summary (one-liner): Run a 3-week POC to validate Redwood inference for Brightlane's product-recommendation reranking pipeline with throughput >= 120 qps and median latency < 85ms at 95th percentile for 1k-token sessions.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail):
- Quality: NDCG@10 improvement >= 6% vs current baseline on provided evaluation set (brightlane_eval_v2.csv).
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 85ms for 1k-token sessions, with <5% timeouts.
- Cost: token cost <= $0.0009 per generated token at target throughput after batching.
- Stability: zero unplanned terminations in 72-hour soak test at 120 qps.

Timeline (target):
- Week 0 (this week): Confirm data access + SSO and share eval dataset (action: Brightlane).
- Week 1: Ingest data, baseline eval, initial model selection + quantization profile (action: Redwood infra + ML).
- Week 2: Integration with Brightlane dev environment, soak test at target throughput, collect telemetry.
- Week 3: Final evaluation, handoff notes, and decision meeting.

Ownership:
- Redwood ENG lead: Sean Gallagher (infra/serving).
- Redwood Success / AE: Aditya Rao (commercial + contract).
- Redwood POC lead: Rachel Kim (technical PM / coordination).
- Brightlane technical lead: Maya Turner.

Immediate asks for Brightlane:
1) SFTP or temporary GCS path with representative product catalog + click logs (anonymized acceptable) by EOD Wednesday.
2) A short security contact for the SOC2 questionnaire (PDF) so we can share the Private options if needed.
3) Confirm the internal decision date target (are you aiming for EOY?)

Risks and first-order mitigations (compact):
- Risk A: Long-sequence latency regressions under production distribution (blocking). Mitigation: We'll run a parallel model variant with reduced context window and KV-cache optimizations; we will also enable prefix caching and a fallback short-context model if p95 > 85ms.
- Risk B: Data residency/compliance requirements. Mitigation: Offer Redwood Private (VPC) evaluation and validate required controls; Lauren to run compliance checklist.
- Risk C: Missing telemetry or instrumentation from Brightlane side. Mitigation: Provide a lightweight agent + logging schema; minimum required fields listed in the attachment.

Escalation path (if blocking):
1) On-call infra (Sean Gallagher) -> 2) POC lead (Rachel Kim) -> 3) AE (Aditya Rao) -> 4) Ops/Eng Director if unresolved within 8 business hours. Also filed INF-4872 in our tracker for the long-sequence latency investigation.

Next steps: please confirm the data delivery plan and a security POC contact. If all good, we'll schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (engineering + infra + product) — proposed slots attached via calendar link.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment stubs: Brightlane-POC-charter-v1.pdf (8 pages), brightlane-sample-schema.csv (2.1 KB)

From: Maya Turner <maya@brightlane.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@brightlane.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Brightlane POC engagement charter & risk compact

Thanks Rachel — this is very clear and appreciated. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: We agree on NDCG target and would like an additional check for latency under cold-cache scenarios (first-request P95). Can Redwood include that as a sub-criterion?
- Security contact: our InfoSec lead is Carlos Vega (cc'd). He will run the SOC2 scan and send the questionnaire by tomorrow.
- Data delivery: we can provision a temporary GCS bucket with anonymized logs, target delivery Wednesday 18:00 PST.

One internal note: our procurement timeline is tight — we have a board review the second week of December. If the POC demonstrates the expected gains, we'll accelerate procurement.

Happy to proceed with the proposed kickoff once we confirm the security questionnaire.

—Maya
Maya Turner
Head of Data Science, Brightlane
maya@brightlane.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@brightlane.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Brightlane POC engagement charter & risk compact

Appreciate the quick turn, Maya — yes, we can add the cold-cache P95 check to the pass/fail criteria (I'll update the charter and reattach). A couple of operational notes and assignments after internal sync: 

- Sean (infra): please confirm the fallback variant and a runbook to flip to short-context model under high p95. If we face memory pressure for 1k-token sessions, we should have the fallback pre-loaded to avoid cold-starts. (Filed as INF-4872).
- Aditya: I'll need you to draft the commercial POC addendum (standard 3-week terms + limited data use) so we can get legal eyes early.
- Lauren: please run the compliance checklist against Brightlane's stated residency requirement (Carlos please confirm whether EU-only or US-only).

Blocking-risk mitigation (detailed):
- If p95 > 85ms on production-like ingest and remediation cannot be completed within 4 business hours, we will: 1) switch traffic to pre-warmed short-context variant, 2) reduce batch window temporarily, 3) notify Brightlane and open an incident with priority P1. If the incident remains open after 8 business hours, follow escalation path in the charter.

I've attached an updated one-page charter (Brightlane-POC-charter-v1.pdf, v1.1 will follow after we confirm cold-cache metric).

Rachel

Attachment stubs: Brightlane-POC-charter-v1.pdf (updated first page), updated plan will be attached after security confirmation.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Brightlane POC engagement charter & risk compact

Looping in a brief compliance note from my review: Brightlane called out potential EU-only residency for click logs. If that's confirmed, we need to validate our EU region Private deployment checklist and a short data flow diagram. I've attached the compliance checklist (redwood-compliance-checklist.pdf) and flagged two items: local logging retention policy and KMS key residency.

Recommendation: If Brightlane requires EU-only storage, propose a short trial on Redwood Private in eu-west-1 for the soak test portion (Week 2). It adds complexity but reduces legal friction. We should include estimated effort and a delta in commercial terms.

Lauren
Director, Product Compliance

Attachment stubs: redwood-compliance-checklist.pdf (3 pages)
